correctness.rationale: All inputs are units modulo 36 and the target gcd class is exactly {6,30}. The explicit twelve-term witness avoids that class even with unrestricted subsequence lengths, giving both lower bounds. Multiplication by a unit normalizes a term to 1 and preserves the gcd predicate. Every sorted normalized bad multiset appears in the unrestricted-depth recursive exact subset-sum-set enumeration, using each old B_{j-1} and testing all unit successors. A complete search visits precisely 3944 bad-prefix nodes, with counts (1,10,47,141,322,560,638,639,633,566,315,72) at depths 1..12 and no depth-13 node. Both exact-set Python and an independently implemented bitmask DFS reproduced the bound. This establishes eta<=13, while D<=eta and the witness yields both constants equal to 13.

originality.rationale: The first public source arXiv:2607.11313v1 defines the exact constants and explicitly asks for composite n with at least two prime divisors. It gives a twelve-term counterexample lower bound at n=6, not the matching upper bound. Source full text, adjacent abstracts, six targeted semantic searches and web searches, and accessible prior claims yielded no theorem implying eta_6^times<=13. Nearest related s1(4) computations and non-divisibility-only constants have inequivalent hypotheses and conclusions; residual independent-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: Gao--Jiang--Mu explicitly pose the pair of local gcd-exact constants for every n with multiple prime factors. n=6 is the first such modulus, and the natural exact invariant has the sharp 13 answer, matching the only known general composite lower bound. The result uses simultaneous 2- and 3-adic avoidance constraints and closes a genuine finite cutoff with a complete, small, checkable certificate, instead of a routine special case of the source prime-power theorem. No broader general formula is claimed.
